**This is a pre-release for testing.** It is not marked Latest and is not intended for general use. If you want a stable build, use [v0.4.8](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/releases/tag/v0.4.8).

This is the third release candidate for 0.5.0. **The features are final:** anything that changes between this build and 0.5.0 is a bug fix. If this build behaves the way you would expect 0.5.0 to, please tell us that too.

rc.3 finishes the macOS **installer packages** that rc.2 introduced: the Installer now explains macFUSE before it installs, shows the license, and ends with what to do next. Nothing else differs from rc.2. Download the `.pkg`, open it, and `xearthlayer` is installed, with no terminal and no first run check.

| Platform | Download |
|---|---|
| Linux x86_64 (glibc 2.34 or newer) | `xearthlayer-v0.5.0-rc.3-x86_64-linux.tar.gz` |
| macOS, Apple Silicon | `xearthlayer-v0.5.0-rc.3-arm64-macos.pkg`, Homebrew (below), or `xearthlayer-v0.5.0-rc.3-arm64-macos.tar.gz` |

No `.deb`, `.rpm` or AUR package is built for previews. There is no Intel Mac build; Intel Mac users can build from source. The `xearthlayer-publish` downloads are the package publishing tool, which testers do not need.

---

## Setup

Close X-Plane and stop any running XEarthLayer before you start.

### 1. Install the binary

**Linux:**

```bash
tar xzf xearthlayer-v0.5.0-rc.3-x86_64-linux.tar.gz
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
mv xearthlayer ~/.local/bin/
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.0-rc.3
```

**macOS:** install [macFUSE](https://macfuse.io) first, including the one-time approval of its system extension. [docs/macos.md](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/blob/develop/0.5.0/docs/macos.md) walks through it. Then choose **one** of the three ways below.

**With the installer package.** Download `xearthlayer-v0.5.0-rc.3-arm64-macos.pkg`, double-click it and follow the Installer. It puts `xearthlayer` in `/usr/local/bin`, which is already on your `PATH`. The package is signed and notarized with the ticket attached, so it installs without a network connection and the command runs straight away. In a new terminal:

```bash
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.0-rc.3
```

To remove it later: `sudo rm /usr/local/bin/xearthlayer` and `sudo pkgutil --forget net.defreyssi.xearthlayer`.

**With Homebrew.** The pre-release channel follows every alpha, beta and rc build, and `brew upgrade` keeps it current:

```bash
brew install --cask xearthlayer/tap/xearthlayer@prerelease
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.0-rc.3
```

If macFUSE is already installed from its own installer, add `--skip-cask-deps`. Already on the channel? `brew upgrade --cask xearthlayer/tap/xearthlayer@prerelease` is all you need.

**From the tarball.** Safari unpacks the download into a folder for you. With Safari:

```bash
cd ~/Downloads/xearthlayer-v0.5.0-rc.3-arm64-macos
```

With any other browser:

```bash
cd ~/Downloads
tar xzf xearthlayer-v0.5.0-rc.3-arm64-macos.tar.gz
```

Then:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
mv xearthlayer ~/.local/bin/
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.0-rc.3
```

The binary is signed and notarized. The first run needs a network connection, because macOS checks the notarization once. If `xearthlayer` is not found, add `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` to your shell profile and open a new terminal.

**Switching to the installer package from an earlier build?** A copy left in `~/.local/bin` from a tarball, or in `/opt/homebrew/bin` from Homebrew, usually comes first on your `PATH` and keeps answering `xearthlayer`. `which -a xearthlayer` lists every copy; remove the ones you no longer use (`brew uninstall --cask xearthlayer@prerelease` for Homebrew). If `xearthlayer --version` does not print `0.5.0-rc.3`, this is why.

### 2. Coming from beta.1, rc.1 or rc.2?

Install the new binary and you are done: your configuration and packages carry over unchanged, and there is nothing to upgrade. Go to step 6.

### 3. Coming from alpha.1 or alpha.2?

Your configuration and packages carry over. The packages you installed from the staging library are the same releases the v2 library publishes, so there is nothing to reinstall. Bring the configuration up to date:

```bash
xearthlayer config upgrade
```

It points `packages.library_url` at the v2 library (XEarthLayer already reads the v2 library in its place before you run this), and it removes `prefetch.mode`: prefetch is on or off by `prefetch.enabled`, and a configuration that had `mode = disabled` keeps prefetch off. Then go to step 5, or straight to step 6 if you already have the regions you fly.

### 4. Coming from v0.4.8, or new to XEarthLayer?

New to XEarthLayer on this machine? Run `xearthlayer setup`. When it finishes it offers to open the package manager, which takes you to step 5.

Coming from v0.4.8: the first command you run copies your `config.ini` to the platform's standard location (`~/.config/xearthlayer/` on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/XEarthLayer/` on macOS) and may ask you to confirm. Accepting is safe: nothing else is moved, and the old `config.ini` is kept, so v0.4.8 still works if you go back to it. The copy reads the v2 library, and the message says so; the old file keeps the library v0.4.8 can use. Then:

```bash
xearthlayer config upgrade
```

The rebuilt world replaces the old one, and the two must not be installed together. Remove every old package **before installing anything new**:

```bash
xearthlayer packages remove --all --force
xearthlayer packages remove --all --type overlay --force
xearthlayer packages list    # should report no packages installed
```

If you had no overlays, the second line prints `Error: Package manager error: No overlay packages are installed`, which is harmless. There is nothing to clean up by hand in `Custom Scenery`: XEarthLayer rebuilds its entries there every time it starts.

To have each ortho install bring its region's overlays, which is off by default:

```bash
xearthlayer config set packages.auto_install_overlays true
```

You can also change it on the package manager's Settings tab.

### 5. Install the regions you fly

Open the package manager:

```bash
xearthlayer packages
```

Press `2` for the Library, move with the arrow keys, mark regions with `Space`, press `i` and confirm with `y`. Press `3` to watch the downloads and installs. `?` lists every key, and `q` quits. [docs/package-management.md](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/blob/develop/0.5.0/docs/package-management.md) describes it in full.

The command line works as before, and takes several regions at once: `xearthlayer packages install na-canada eu-west`. A region code, or the start of one, installs every package beneath it.

| Region | Covers | Download |
|---|---|---|
| `NA-USA-BERMUDA-BAHAMAS` | Contiguous US, Alaska, Hawaii, Bermuda, the Bahamas, Turks and Caicos | 14.1 GB |
| `NA-MEXICO-CENTRAL` | Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean | 4.5 GB |
| `NA-CANADA-WEST` | Canada west of 95° W | 10.2 GB |
| `NA-CANADA-EAST` | Canada east of 95° W | 13.2 GB |
| `NA-GREENLAND` | Greenland | 0.8 GB |
| `SA-WEST` | Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile, the Guianas | 9.2 GB |
| `SA-EAST` | Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay, the Falklands | 8.8 GB |
| `EU-WEST` | Europe west of Russia, Iceland, Scandinavia, the Mediterranean | 16.1 GB |
| `EU-EAST` | European Russia west of the Urals | 3.7 GB |
| `AF-NORTH` | North and West Africa | 7.3 GB |
| `AF-SOUTH` | Central, East and Southern Africa | 9.1 GB |
| `AS-INDIA-MIDDLE-EAST-HIMALAYAN` | Middle East, Central Asia, the Indian subcontinent | 16.8 GB |
| `AS-CHINA-MONGOLIA` | China and Mongolia | 18.5 GB |
| `AS-ASIA-PACIFIC` | Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Southeast Asia, the Philippines | 11.6 GB |
| `AS-RUSSIA-CENTRAL` | Siberia from the Urals to Lake Baikal | 4.8 GB |
| `AS-RUSSIA-EAST` | The Russian Far East | 6.4 GB |
| `OC-AUSTRALIA-NZ-PACIFIC` | Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific islands | 5.5 GB |

Sizes are download sizes. The whole world is about 161 GB. Antarctica is not available yet.

### 6. Run

```bash
xearthlayer run
```

---

## What changed since rc.2

- **The installer package explains what comes next.** XEarthLayer cannot start without macFUSE, which is a separate install, and the package used to say so only on its first page. Its Read Me page now lists every step: installing macFUSE, allowing kernel extensions in Recovery on Apple Silicon, and approving macFUSE in Privacy & Security. The last page tells you what to do next: run `xearthlayer setup` if macFUSE is ready, or set up macFUSE first. Its links lead to the guides on xearthlayer.app.
- **The license is shown in the Installer.** Both packages show the MIT license, to accept before installing.

Nothing else changed: this is rc.2's code, built again at the new version. rc.2 was the first build with installer packages, and rc.1 carried the same code without them.

---

## What we most want tested

### 1. The macOS installer package

Download the `.pkg` with Safari, the way most people will. Does it open in the Installer without a warning, does it finish, and does `xearthlayer --version` in a new terminal print `0.5.0-rc.3`? If you can, try it once with Wi-Fi turned off: it should install exactly the same. If you are moving from Homebrew or a tarball, tell us whether `which -a` and the note in step 1 were enough to get you onto the new copy.

Read the Installer's pages as you go, especially if this Mac has never had macFUSE: could you follow the Read Me's macFUSE steps from the page alone, and did the last page leave you knowing what to run next?

These two commands show what macOS thinks of the download, and are worth pasting into any report about it:

```bash
pkgutil --check-signature ~/Downloads/xearthlayer-v0.5.0-rc.3-arm64-macos.pkg
spctl --assess --type install -vv ~/Downloads/xearthlayer-v0.5.0-rc.3-arm64-macos.pkg
```

### 2. Your normal flights

This is the build we intend to call 0.5.0. Fly your usual routes with the regions you normally use, and tell us about anything that would stop you recommending it: pauses or purple tiles at DSF boundary crossings, slow starts, missing scenery, night lighting over cities that looks wrong, or SimHeaven X-World Pro misbehaving with `packages.xworld_pro` on.

### 3. The package manager

Installing and deleting regions, the Settings tab, and quitting with `q` while jobs are running. Anything that looks stuck, any row that never finishes, and any key that does not do what `?` says.

### The dashboard

The Status pane leads its lines with emoji. If your terminal shows empty boxes instead, `xearthlayer config set tui.symbols plain` uses plain marks. The default, `auto`, tries to detect this for you.

## How to report

The flight log is `xearthlayer.log`, and the package manager's log is `xearthlayer-packages.log`, both at `~/.local/state/xearthlayer/` on Linux and in `~/Library/Logs/XEarthLayer/` on macOS unless you changed `logging.file`. `xearthlayer run` empties the flight log when it starts, so copy it before the next flight. Then run:

```bash
xearthlayer --version
xearthlayer diagnostics
```

The most useful report is your route, aircraft and flight time, the last few `Prefetch sample` lines from the flight log, and what looked wrong. For a package manager or install problem, say what you pressed and what the screen showed, and attach `xearthlayer-packages.log`. For the installer package, say which browser you downloaded it with and include the output of the two commands in section 1 above.

---

## Known issues, please don't report these

**FUSE read counts on the dashboard are low on macOS.** macOS serves repeat reads of a texture from its own cache, so XEarthLayer only sees the first one. Nothing else depends on that count.

**Saving a setting rewrites `config.ini` from its template.** Comments you added to the file by hand are lost, as they are with `xearthlayer config set`. The values are kept.

**Antarctica is not in the library yet.**
